prompt: Which expression is equivalent to $3x^{-2}$, for $x \neq 0$?
hint: A negative exponent does not make anything negative. Recall what it means for the position of its base in a fraction.

hints.text: A negative exponent does not make anything negative. Recall what it means for the position of its base in a fraction.
The exponent $-2$ belongs only to $x$, so rewrite $x^{-2}$ as $\dfrac{1}{x^2}$. The coefficient $3$ stays where it is, on top.
The expression becomes $3 \cdot \dfrac{1}{x^2} = \dfrac{3}{x^2}$, which is choice B.

learningObjective: Rewrite a negative exponent as a reciprocal.
explanation: A negative exponent flips its base into the denominator: $x^{-2} = \dfrac{1}{x^2}$.
The coefficient $3$ has no negative exponent, so it stays in the numerator: $\dfrac{3}{x^2}$.
Choice A treats the negative exponent as a negative sign. Choice C wrongly moves the $3$ down with the $x$.

alternativeExplanations.title: Only what carries the exponent moves
steps: In $3x^{-2}$ the exponent $-2$ is attached to $x$ only, so only $x^2$ moves to the denominator and the result is $\dfrac{3}{x^2}$.
If the expression were $(3x)^{-2}$, the $3$ would move too and the result would be $\dfrac{1}{9x^2}$, a different expression.
A test with $x = 2$ agrees: $3 \cdot 2^{-2} = \dfrac{3}{4}$, and choice B also gives $\dfrac{3}{4}$.
